ACCUMULATOR_RESET_INSIDE_LOOP.detects: A running total, count or piece of text that is set back to its starting value inside the loop that builds it, so only the last pass counts.
ACCUMULATOR_RESET_INSIDE_LOOP.considers: Every assignment of a literal (0, 1, "") inside a loop to a variable that the same loop also adds to with +=, ++ or similar.
unreliable_when: The reset is meant to happen once per row or group: the model has to infer that from where the value is read, and a per-group total that is only read after the loop looks like the mistake.
The running value is kept in a field or handed to another method, which the model cannot follow.
limitations: Only resets to a literal are considered; total = start; is not checked.

ARRAY_LENGTH_INDEX_MISUSE.detects: An array, String or list read at index length (or length(), size()), one past the last valid position.
ARRAY_LENGTH_INDEX_MISUSE.considers: Every index written as a length minus 0, 1 or 2, directly or through a variable that was set to one and not changed since.
unreliable_when: The index only equals the length because of something computed in another method or a loop the model does not trace.
A collection is replaced by a longer one in a way other than new T[n + 1] in the same method.

CONSTANT_FALSE_LOOP_CONDITION.detects: A for loop whose condition is already false at the first check, so the body never runs.
CONSTANT_FALSE_LOOP_CONDITION.considers: For loops whose start and condition can be compared: two literals (only when the first check fails), counting up from 0 or 1 while i > n, counting below zero, or a condition that compares the counter with its own start.
unreliable_when: The bound is a variable whose value is only known at run time (i > n with n negative is legitimately true).
Loops written as while loops are not considered at all.
limitations: The old rule could only judge two literals, so its F1 on these test sites is 0: almost every test mistake has a length or variable as its bound.

DECIMAL_EQUALITY_COMPARISON.detects: Two double or float values compared with == or !=, which a calculated value often fails by a tiny rounding error.
DECIMAL_EQUALITY_COMPARISON.considers: Every == or != where at least one side is known to be a double or float.
DECIMAL_EQUALITY_COMPARISON.lookalike:
if (divisor == 0.0) return 0;        // deliberate exact check
if (x == Math.floor(x)) { ... }   // is it whole?
unreliable_when: The value was never calculated (read straight from input and compared with the same literal), where == happens to be safe.
The type of one side cannot be worked out from the file, e.g. a method declared in another class.
limitations: Labelled by construction (a planted == on decimals is a mistake by definition), because test inputs rarely hit the exact rounding case.
Two of the 19 correct-code sites in the test split were flagged (precision 0.93).

DIVISION_BY_ZERO_LITERAL.detects: A whole-number division or remainder whose divisor can be zero when the line runs, which crashes with an ArithmeticException.
DIVISION_BY_ZERO_LITERAL.considers: Integer divisions by the literal 0, by a length or size, by a parameter, by a variable that starts at 0, or by an alias of a length. Other divisors are not proposed.
unreliable_when: The divisor is guarded in a way the model does not recognise, such as a check in the caller or an early return in another method.
The divisor is computed (gcd(a, b), n - k): these are not proposed, so such crashes are not found.
limitations: The detector it replaced only knew the literal 0, which none of the test mistakes use, so that detector scores 0 here.

EARLY_RETURN_IN_LOOP.detects: A loop that returns on its first pass whatever happens, usually an else return false; inside a search, so only the first element is ever checked.
EARLY_RETURN_IN_LOOP.considers: Loops whose body ends in a return, or contains an if/else where both branches return, break or throw.
unreliable_when: The loop is deliberately one pass, e.g. returning the first element of a non-empty list.
Almost every proposed site in the test split is a real mistake (141 of 144), so the score says little about telling look-alikes apart.
limitations: Mutants that make the return unconditional are labelled by construction.

EMPTY_CONDITIONAL_BODY.detects: A semicolon right after an if, while or for header, which makes the body empty so the condition controls nothing.
EMPTY_CONDITIONAL_BODY.considers: Every if, while or for whose body is a lone ; or an empty { }.
EMPTY_CONDITIONAL_BODY.lookalike:
int i = 0;
for (; i < n && a[i] != key; i++);   // the header does the work
unreliable_when: An empty-bodied loop is used on purpose and written on one line, which the model has seen less of than the mistake.

IGNORED_STRING_METHOD_RESULT.detects: A String method such as trim() or toUpperCase() called as a statement, whose new value is thrown away because Strings never change in place.
IGNORED_STRING_METHOD_RESULT.considers: Every statement that is only a call to a String or StringBuilder method on some value.
IGNORED_STRING_METHOD_RESULT.lookalike:
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(word);
sb.reverse();          // changes sb itself
unreliable_when: The receiver's type is declared in another file, so the model cannot tell a String from a builder.
limitations: Labelled by construction (a dropped String result is a mistake by definition).

INCORRECT_CONDITIONAL_OPERATOR.detects: An assignment (=) written where a comparison (==) was meant, inside a condition.
INCORRECT_CONDITIONAL_OPERATOR.considers: Every assignment inside the condition of an if, while, do, for or ?:.
unreliable_when: The assignment is to a boolean and is meant (rare, but legal).
limitations: Only 5 of the 38 test sites are look-alikes, so precision rests on few cases.

INDEX_PLUS_ONE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS.detects: A[i + 1] (or a[i - 1]) inside a loop that lets i reach the last (or first) index, so the neighbour is out of bounds.
INDEX_PLUS_ONE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS.considers: Every index of the form counter + k or counter - k inside a counted for loop.
unreliable_when: The access is guarded by an if or a break the model does not recognise.
While loops and for-each loops are not considered.
limitations: Recall is 0.90: the threshold was set for precision, so about 1 in 10 of these mistakes in the test split is not flagged.

INTEGER_DIVISION_IN_DECIMAL_CONTEXT.detects: Two whole numbers divided where a decimal result was wanted, e.g. an average stored in a double, so the remainder is lost first.
INTEGER_DIVISION_IN_DECIMAL_CONTEXT.considers: Every division where both sides are int or char; where the value goes decides it.
INTEGER_DIVISION_IN_DECIMAL_CONTEXT.lookalike:
int middle = (low + high) / 2;
int tens = n / 10 % 10;
unreliable_when: The value goes somewhere the model cannot see the type of (a method in another class, a collection).
Dropping the remainder is intended but the result is still stored in a double.

LOOP_COUNTER_CHANGED_IN_BODY.detects: A for loop's counter changed inside the body as well as in the header, so elements are skipped or repeated.
LOOP_COUNTER_CHANGED_IN_BODY.considers: Every write to a for loop's counter inside its body (not counting a nested loop's own header).
unreliable_when: Skipping ahead is deliberate (parsing, run-length counting) and the reason is not visible in a nearby if.
While loops are not considered: there the counter is meant to change in the body.
limitations: Precision is 0.85, the lowest of the 24.

LOOP_SKIPS_LAST_ELEMENT.detects: A loop that stops one element early (i < a.length - 1) while the body only uses a[i], so the last element is never processed.
LOOP_SKIPS_LAST_ELEMENT.considers: Every counted for loop whose bound is a length minus one (or that starts at length - 1 and counts down to 0).
unreliable_when: The last element is handled after the loop, which the model only partly sees.
Nested loops such as bubble sort, where the inner bound depends on the outer counter.

LOOP_UPDATE_WRONG_DIRECTION.detects: A for loop whose update moves the counter away from its bound (i < n with i--), so the loop never finishes or ends with an error.
LOOP_UPDATE_WRONG_DIRECTION.considers: Every counted for loop that compares its counter with a bound using <, <=, > or >=.
unreliable_when: The body also changes the counter or leaves the loop in a way that makes the header's direction irrelevant.

MISLEADING_INDENTATION_NO_BRACES.detects: A second line indented under an if, else or loop that has no braces, which looks like part of the body but always runs.
MISLEADING_INDENTATION_NO_BRACES.considers: Every if, else or loop without braces, together with the statement that follows it.
unreliable_when: The file mixes tabs and spaces, so the indentation the model reads differs from what the editor shows.
The code was auto-formatted, which removes the evidence.
limitations: Labelled by construction (a planted indented line after a braceless body is a mistake by definition).

MISSING_BREAK_IN_SWITCH.detects: A switch case without break that runs on into the next case when that changes the result.
MISSING_BREAK_IN_SWITCH.considers: Every case group that does not end in break, return, throw or continue and is followed by another case.
unreliable_when: The fall-through is intended but has no comment saying so and does not follow the build-up pattern above.
Switch expressions and arrow cases (case 1 -> ...) cannot fall through and are not considered.

NESTED_LOOP_WRONG_COUNTER.detects: A for loop header that tests or updates the wrong counter, usually the outer loop's i instead of j.
NESTED_LOOP_WRONG_COUNTER.considers: Every for loop whose condition or update does not mention the variable it declares.
NESTED_LOOP_WRONG_COUNTER.lookalike:
for (int i = 0, j = n - 1; i < j; i++, j--)
    swap(a, i, j);
unreliable_when: The loop is deliberately driven by another variable (two-pointer loops written unusually).
limitations: Almost every proposed site in the test split is a real mistake (92 of 97), so the score says little about telling look-alikes apart.

NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT_OPERATOR.detects: & or | between two conditions where && or || was needed, so the right side runs even when the left already decided, e.g. s.length() after s != null.
NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT_OPERATOR.considers: Every & or | between two boolean expressions.
NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT_OPERATOR.lookalike: if (a > 0 & b > 0) { ... }   // no side effects, same result
unreliable_when: The right side is guarded somewhere the model does not look, e.g. a field checked in the constructor.
limitations: There are no correct-code sites in the test split: every look-alike is a planted & or | that behaved the same. The model was trained to treat those as fine, which is right for students but not a style check.

OFF_BY_ONE_LOOP_BOUNDARY.detects: A loop that runs one step too far, e.g. i <= a.length, so the last pass indexes past the end.
OFF_BY_ONE_LOOP_BOUNDARY.considers: Every counted for loop that compares its counter with <= (or >= when counting down from the length), or with < against a bound past the length, unless the bound already subtracts from the length.
unreliable_when: The bound is a variable whose relation to an array's length is set elsewhere.
While loops are not considered.
limitations: One of the 7 correct-code sites in the test split was flagged.

STRING_EQUALITY_WITH_OPERATOR.detects: Two Strings compared with == or !=, which compares which object they are, not their text.
STRING_EQUALITY_WITH_OPERATOR.considers: Every == or != where one side is, or might be, a String or other object and neither side is null.
STRING_EQUALITY_WITH_OPERATOR.lookalike:
if (answer.equals("yes")) { ... }
if (c == 'y') { ... }        // a char, not a String
unreliable_when: One side's type cannot be worked out (a method from another class); the model then relies on how the comparison is written.
limitations: Labelled by construction (== between two Strings is a mistake by definition).
Recall is 0.81: it misses comparisons whose String type it cannot see.

UNREACHABLE_ELSE_IF_ORDER.detects: An else-if chain whose earlier test already covers a later one (>= 50 before >= 75), so the later branch can never run.
UNREACHABLE_ELSE_IF_ORDER.considers: If/else-if chains of two or more branches that compare the same variable with numbers.
UNREACHABLE_ELSE_IF_ORDER.mistake:
if (mark >= 50) grade = 'C';
else if (mark >= 75) grade = 'A';   // never reached
unreliable_when: The conditions compare against variables or method results, whose values the model cannot order.

WHILE_VARIABLE_NOT_UPDATED.detects: A while loop whose condition never changes inside the loop, so it may never end.
WHILE_VARIABLE_NOT_UPDATED.considers: Every while and do-while loop whose condition uses at least one variable, unless that variable is changed through a method call such as remove() or next().
unreliable_when: The condition changes through a field, another method or another object.
The loop is left by break or return, which the model weighs but cannot always confirm happens.
limitations: Recall is 0.89: about 1 in 9 of these mistakes in the test split is not flagged.

WRONG_EXTREME_INITIAL_VALUE.detects: A maximum or minimum search that starts from a value that can beat every element, e.g. int min = 0 when all values are positive.
WRONG_EXTREME_INITIAL_VALUE.considers: Every variable that a loop keeps as the largest or smallest value seen, together with its starting value.
WRONG_EXTREME_INITIAL_VALUE.mistake:
int min = 0;
for (int x : values) if (x < min) min = x;
unreliable_when: Whether 0 is a safe start depends on the data, which the model only sees through names and how the values are produced.
limitations: One of the 43 correct-code sites in the test split was flagged.

WRONG_LOOP_VARIABLE_IN_INDEX.detects: An inner loop that indexes with the outer loop's counter (a[i] where a[j] was meant).
WRONG_LOOP_VARIABLE_IN_INDEX.considers: Every index inside an inner for loop that uses an outer loop's counter.
unreliable_when: Using the outer counter is intended and the inner counter is used elsewhere in the same statement.
limitations: The weakest model of the 24: F1 0.87, precision 0.87, recall 0.88. CodeBERT scored higher here (0.90).
